title: Irregular potentials: 見える and 聞こえる
summary: 見られる and 聞ける are the regular potentials; 見える and 聞こえる are forced self-move forms that mean "look like" and "sound like".

blocks.text: Japanese is very regular. The few irregularities are local: a verb that is regular almost everywhere and bends in one spot. 見る and 聞く are two of them, and the bend has a reason.

The ichidan potential is **られる** and the godan potential is **え-stem + る**. 見れる, with the ら dropped, is a common speech habit (ら抜き). Many people still treat it as incorrect, and the course says to keep 見られる in your own writing. It is not a new verb.

Potentials are mostly **self-move**: 本が読める, "the book does readable". But the regular 見られる and 聞ける can also be other-move in describing clauses: さくらを見られる日 ("the day I can see Sakura") has an object. The irregular **見える** and **聞こえる** can only be self-move. They cannot take an object.

A small shade of meaning separates them from their regular partners. 見える is physical ability: it comes into view. 見られる suggests having the opportunity. If the tall lady in front takes off her hat, 芝居が見える. If tickets are on sale, 芝居が見られる.
Why they survive: looks like, sounds like

The real reason they exist is that **how something looks or sounds** is always self-move: it is the thing that appears, not something we do to it. So the forced forms became the "looks like / sounds like" verbs. A noun takes **に**, an い-adjective takes the **く-stem**.

blocks.en: That cloud looks like a dog.

blocks.jp: その話は変に聞こえる。
遠くから鐘の音が聞こえる。
blocks.en: A bell can be heard from far away.

items: Regular potentials: **見られる** (ichidan), **聞ける** (godan); 見れる is spoken ら抜き.
**見える** and **聞こえる** are forced self-move: no object.
**Nに見える**, **く-stem + 見える**, **Nに / adverb + 聞こえる** = looks / sounds like.
見える is physical visibility; 見られる suggests having the chance.

questions.prompt: さくらはカエル＿＿見える。 (Sakura looks like a frog.)

questions.prompt: 見える can be used with を in さくらを見える日.
questions.note: Use さくらを見られる日; 見える cannot take を.
聞こえた is the forced self-move form that means sounds.
